item.title: PFIZENMAIER ON HEALTH COSTS
item.description: Taking care of yourself is the key to living a healthy and long life. For many people, one excuse for not following through with regular doctor check ups is saying they can’t afford it. Franklin County Health Department Director Brenda Pfizenmaier says there are ways to afford screenings and appointments: Don’t put off regular doctor visits and check ups. Contact the health department or your doctor to get a check up or screening schedule today.

item.title: WELLSVILLE AND EV CHARGING STATIONS
item.description: The City of Wellsville is looking into installing electric vehicle charging stations somewhere in the city. At the Wellsville City Council meeting recently, Franklin County Development Council Director Paul Bean discussed a way to finance them: The council agreed to study the situation and decide where they would like to install the EV charging stations, and how many. That way they could plan some of the cost into next year’s budget.

item.title: IDITAROD STARTS IN ALASKA
item.description: On of the longest, most brutal competitions in the world started this weekend. Called the Last Great Race on Earth, the Iditarod, a 1,000 mile dog sled race from Anchorage to Nome, Alaska. Every team starts the run with exactly 12 dogs through downtown Anchorage. There are 37 teams competing this year, including 11 women. There are 444 sled dogs running the race. The ceremonial start in Anchorage does not count toward the race time.
